over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Fortress Investment Group LLC realized record after acquisition by SoftBank Group Corp., ~3-5-year horizon (~2020-2022)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. The acquired entity deregistered from SEC
> reporting shortly after closing and its Japan-based acquirer does not itself file
> periodic reports with the SEC, so no primary-source financial record exists for the
> fixed outcome window; realized-record facts here are limited to what a public search
> of SEC EDGAR could establish and to reputable secondary press. This sub-dossier
> contains no information about how the transaction was structured or negotiated.

## Public-reporting status through the outcome window
- On January 8, 2018, Fortress Investment Group LLC filed a Form 15-12B certifying
  termination of registration of its Class A Shares under Section 12(g) of the
  Exchange Act, reporting approximately one (1) holder of record as of the
  certification date. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-18-004978, Form 15-12B]
- A review of the registrant's (CIK 0001380393) EDGAR filing history for 2018 through
  2022 shows no Form 10-K, 20-F, or other periodic report filed after the Form 15-12B;
  the last periodic filing on record is the fiscal-year-2016 Form 10-K filed
  February 28, 2017, before the merger closed. [SRC: https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001380393&type=10-K&dateb=&owner=include&count=40]
- A search of SEC EDGAR company records for "SoftBank" (the acquirer, Softbank Group
  Corp., a Japanese kabushiki kaisha) returns no matching registrant of any filing type,
  indicating SoftBank Group Corp. does not itself file periodic reports (e.g., Form
  20-F or 10-K) with the SEC and has not made a separate SEC disclosure of the acquired
  business's post-closing segment results. [SRC: https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&company=softbank&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=100]
- Consequently, no SEC-filed financial statements, revenue, net income/loss, or other
  audited scalar exists for this entity within the fixed ~2020-2022 outcome window;
  the realized financial trajectory cannot be established from a primary filing.
  [UNVERIFIED]

## Realized business record noted in reputable secondary press (window-dated)
- Reporting dated November 1, 2021 (Bloomberg News, republished by Al Jazeera and other
  outlets) states that "[s]ince the transaction closed in December 2017, Fortress has
  been run independently," and that, "[t]o win approval from the Committee on Foreign
  Investment in the U.S., SoftBank agreed to cede any control of day-to-day operations
  of Fortress." [SRC: https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2021/11/1/softbank-mulls-sale-of-fortress-investment-group]
- The same report states that SoftBank Group Corp. was, as of that date, "considering a
  sale of Fortress Investment Group as the Japanese conglomerate reviews options for the
  asset manager," attributing the review in part to the acquirer's having been "unable
  to mesh Fortress's operations with its own," with discussions described as at an
  early stage. [SRC: https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2021/11/1/softbank-mulls-sale-of-fortress-investment-group]
- The report states the three founding Principals (Briger, Edens, Nardone) continued to
  be identified as the entity's founders, and cites the entity's own website as
  reporting $53.9 billion in assets under management as of June 30, 2021 across credit,
  private equity, and permanent-capital vehicles. [SRC: https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2021/11/1/softbank-mulls-sale-of-fortress-investment-group]

## Items noted but not primary-verifiable
- The $53.9 billion AUM figure attributed to the entity's own website (as of June 30,
  2021) is a company self-report relayed through press, not an audited SEC-filed
  figure, and is recorded here as [UNVERIFIED] for scalar-verification purposes.
  [UNVERIFIED]
- Subsequent press reporting (2023) describes a definitive agreement for Fortress
  management together with Mubadala Capital to acquire SoftBank's stake in the entity,
  with completion reported in 2024 — both dates fall outside the fixed ~2020-2022
  outcome window and are noted only for completeness, not as within-window outcome
  facts. [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Because the acquired entity deregistered from SEC reporting in January 2018 and its
  acquirer does not separately file with the SEC, no public, audited 3-5-year financial
  record exists for this entity; the outcome is coded uncertain on any financial-scalar
  basis. The only within-window realized-record information available is qualitative
  and press-sourced (not primary-filed): as of November 2021, reputable press reported
  the business continuing to operate under its pre-existing leadership with
  contractually preserved day-to-day operating independence from its acquirer, while
  the same reporting noted the acquirer was reviewing strategic options including a
  sale, attributed in part to difficulty integrating the acquired business's operations
  with its own. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-18-004978, Form 15-12B] [SRC: https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2021/11/1/softbank-mulls-sale-of-fortress-investment-group]

[SLICE END]
